definition_zh: 吸收；同化；使相似；逐渐融入
definition_en: to take something in and make it part of a larger whole, or to become like that whole
core_image: 一块冰放进温水，边界一点点消失，最后整杯水都带着它的凉意
scene: 身体把一碗饭变成力气，学生把新公式接进旧知识，新来的邻居慢慢学会本地口音。It took the newcomer a decade to assimilate the local customs and speech.
sceneCN: 这里 assimilate 指「吸收并融入当地习俗与语言」（第 1 个义项：把外部事物纳入自身并使之一致）；句意为这个新来者花了十年才吸收并融入当地的习俗与说话方式。可辨识物件：饭碗、课本、街区门廊、口音示意。

pos.zh: 吸收（营养、知识）；使同化；使相似

senses.title: Absorb nutrients
senses.definition: to take food or a substance into the body and convert it into usable material
senses.definitionCN: 把食物或物质纳入身体并转化为可用物质
senses.example: The body assimilates iron more easily when vitamin C is present.
senses.exampleCN: 有维生素配合时，身体更容易吸收铁。
senses.why: The oldest concrete sense: the body makes foreign matter into its own substance.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的具体义：身体把外来物质变成自身物质。

senses.title: Absorb and understand information
senses.definition: to take in ideas or information until they become part of one's understanding
senses.definitionCN: 把观念或信息纳入，使其成为理解的一部分
senses.example: Students need time to assimilate the new material before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 学生需要时间在考试前吸收新材料。
senses.why: The mind repeats the body's work: what is taken in must be broken down and rebuilt as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 心智重复身体的工作：纳入之物必须被拆解并重建为自己所有。

senses.title: Become part of a group or culture
senses.definition: to become absorbed into a community and take on its ways, often used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 被一个社群吸收并接受其生活方式，常不带宾语
senses.example: Many newcomers assimilate within a generation and keep little of the old tongue.
senses.exampleCN: 许多新来者在一代人之内融入，只留下很少的旧语言。
senses.why: Here the person is both the thing absorbed and the agent of change, which is why the verb can stand alone.
senses.whyCN: 这里的人既是被吸收之物，也是变化的行为者，因此这个动词可以单独使用。

senses.title: Make one thing like another
senses.definition: to make something resemble something else, often with 'to' in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 使某物与另一物相似，正式文体中常用介词引出比较对象
senses.example: The reform assimilates local practice to the national model.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革使本地做法向全国模式靠拢。
senses.why: This transitive pattern keeps the Latin frame: one thing is made like another, and the direction is explicit.
senses.whyCN: 这个及物结构保留拉丁框架：一物被弄得像另一物，方向明确。

senses.title: Assimilate a speech sound
senses.definition: to change a sound so that it becomes more like a neighbouring sound
senses.definitionCN: 改变一个语音，使其更接近相邻语音
senses.example: In rapid speech, speakers assimilate the final nasal to the following consonant.
senses.exampleCN: 在快速语流中，说话人让词尾鼻音向后续辅音同化。
senses.why: Sounds are the smallest things that can be absorbed: one phoneme borrows a feature from its neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 语音是可以被吸收的最小事物：一个音位从邻居借来一个特征。

senses.title: Absorb into an organization
senses.definition: to merge a smaller unit into a larger structure so that it operates as part of it
senses.definitionCN: 把较小单位并入较大结构，使其作为其中一部分运作
senses.example: The agency assimilated the smaller office into its own structure.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构把较小的办事处并入自己的架构。
senses.why: Institutions use the verb for mergers, because a merged unit is expected to adopt the parent's procedures.
senses.whyCN: 机构用这个动词指合并，因为被并入的单位被期望采用母体的程序。

senses.title: Digest an experience
senses.definition: to process a difficult experience until it can be understood and carried
senses.definitionCN: 处理艰难经历，直到它能被理解并承受
senses.example: Children assimilate difficult events through play and repeated stories.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童通过游戏与反复讲述来消化艰难事件。
senses.why: The psychological sense treats experience as food: it must be taken in slowly before it can nourish.
senses.whyCN: 心理义把经验当作食物：必须慢慢纳入，才能滋养人。

senses.title: Absorb a people or territory by force
senses.definition: to bring a people or region under control and erase its separate identity
senses.definitionCN: 把民族或地区纳入控制并抹去其独立身份
senses.example: The empire assimilated the border province over several decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这个帝国用几十年时间吞并了边境省份。
senses.why: Power uses the same word as digestion: to assimilate a people is to consume them as a body consumes food.
senses.whyCN: 权力使用与消化相同的词：同化一个民族，就是像身体消化食物那样吞并它。

intro.en: Assimilate comes from Latin assimilare 'to make like, to absorb', from ad- 'to' and similis 'like'. It entered English through French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: assimilate 来自拉丁 assimilare「使相似、吸收」，由 ad-「向」与 similis「相似」构成，经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Similis meant 'like, similar'. It is generally connected with simul 'together', but the pre-Latin shape is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: similis 意为「相似的」。一般认为与 simul「一起」同源，但拉丁语之前的形态属重构形式，并无实际书证。

items.en: Ad- 'to, toward' plus similis gave assimilare 'to make like, to liken, to absorb'.
items.cn: ad-「向、朝」加 similis 构成 assimilare「使相似、比作、吸收」。

items.en: The verb entered English in the sixteenth century through French, first meaning 'to make similar'.
items.cn: 这个动词在十六世纪经法语进入英语，最初意为「使相似」。

items.en: Physiology applied it to food becoming tissue, and psychology to new experience becoming part of a schema.
items.cn: 生理学用它指食物变成组织，心理学用它指新经验成为图式的一部分。

items.en: Modern sociology uses it for newcomers becoming like a host society, and linguistics for neighbouring sounds becoming alike.
items.cn: 现代社会学用它指新来者变得像主流社会，语言学用它指相邻语音变得相似。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the connection of similis to simul is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin form is reconstructed, and the first date of each technical sense is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：similis 与 simul 的联系虽被一般接受，但其拉丁语之前形态属重构形式；各技术义的首见年代无法确定。

note.en: Group one shares the 'like' root; group two holds verbs of taking something in.
note.cn: 第一组共享「相似」词根；第二组是表示纳入某物的动词。

entries.definition: The process or result; the verb names the act that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或结果；动词指产生它的动作。

entries.definition: Describes someone or something already absorbed.
entries.definitionCN: 描述已被吸收的人或物。

entries.definition: Describes the capacity to absorb or make similar.
entries.definitionCN: 描述吸收或同化的能力。

entries.definition: To make unlike or to become less similar; the prefix reverses the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 使不同或变得不相似；前缀反转了方向。

entries.definition: The general verb for taking in liquid, heat or knowledge; it does not say the thing is remade.
entries.definitionCN: 指吸收液体、热量或知识的普通动词，不表示纳入之物被改造。

entries.definition: To bring parts into a working whole; it stresses structure more than likeness.
entries.definitionCN: 指把各部分带入一个运作整体，强调结构而非相似。

entries.definition: To break food or information down into usable form; assimilate stresses the later incorporation.
entries.definitionCN: 指把食物或信息分解为可用形式；assimilate 强调其后的并入。

entries.definition: To include something as part of a body or company; it is often organizational.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物作为身体或公司的一部分纳入，常用于组织语境。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real verb forms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实动词形式，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ad- 'toward' plus similis 'like': to move toward likeness.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 similis「相似」：朝相似移动。

normal.en: The verb family runs assimilate, assimilates, assimilated, assimilating, assimilation.
Fixed phrases: assimilate nutrients, assimilate information, assimilate into society.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：吸收营养、吸收信息、融入社会。

normal.en: The intransitive use describes people; the transitive use can describe food, facts or sounds.
normal.cn: 不及物用法描述人；及物用法可描述食物、事实或语音。

normal.en: Spelling note: the prefix ends in a voiced stop, but writing has merged it into the following hissing sound.
normal.cn: 注意双写的咝音：前缀末辅音在书写中已与后面的咝音合并。

abstract.en: Picture a cube of ice losing its edge in warm water.
abstract.cn: 想象一块冰在温水里失去棱角。

abstract.en: Picture a new song becoming hummable in a foreign key.
abstract.cn: 想象一首新歌在异国调子里变得随口可哼。

abstract.en: Picture a river carrying silt until the silt is simply part of the water.
abstract.cn: 想象河流携着泥沙，直到泥沙干脆成为水的一部分。

examples.en: It takes years to assimilate a second language well enough to joke in it.
examples.cn: 要把第二语言吸收到能开玩笑的程度，需要多年。

examples.en: The body cannot assimilate the mineral without enough fat in the diet.
examples.cn: 饮食中脂肪不足时，身体无法吸收这种矿物质。

examples.en: The new department was assimilated into the older one within a year.
examples.cn: 新部门在一年内被并入较老的部门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「朝向」加「相似」加「使……」——使外来的东西变得像自己

root: 拉丁 assimilare「使相似、吸收」= ad-（向）+ similis（相似），经法语进入英语。similis 一般认为与 simul「一起」同源，更早形态属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one intake: something outside is brought in and made to fit, whether it is food, information, a person, a sound, an office, an experience or a conquered people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次纳入展开：外部之物被带进来并被弄得合身，它可以是食物、信息、人、语音、机构、经历或被征服的民族。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece of ice dissolving in warm water until the whole glass carries its coolness.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块冰在温水中消融，直到整杯水都带着它的凉意。

branches.en: FOOD FIRST: the body turns foreign matter into tissue.
branches.cn: 食物在先：身体把外来物质变成组织。

branches.en: MIND: information and painful experience must be broken down before they become one's own.
branches.cn: 心智：信息与痛苦经历必须先被拆解，才能成为自己所有。

branches.en: PERSON AND GROUP: a newcomer becomes like the host without losing the ability to act.
branches.cn: 人与群体：新来者变得像主流，却不失行动能力。

branches.en: LIKENESS AND SOUND: one thing is made like another, down to a single phoneme.
branches.cn: 相似与语音：一物被弄得像另一物，小到一个音位。

branches.en: POWER: an office is merged, and a people can be swallowed by an empire.
branches.cn: 权力：机构被合并，民族也能被帝国吞并。

intro.en: Assimilate is a Latin verb of direction plus likeness, with a family of English nouns, adjectives and a reversed form.
intro.cn: assimilate 是一个由方向前缀与「相似」构成的拉丁动词，并有一族英语名词、形容词与一个反向形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis supplies similar and similarity; ad- turns the adjective into a verb of making, and dis- reverses it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 similis 衍生 similar 与 similarity；ad- 把这个形容词变成「使……」的动词，dis- 则反转方向。

items.example: The prefix aims the action at a target.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向目标。

items.example: The verb names the act of making one thing like another.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指使一物像另一物。

items.example: Assimilation can be cultural or physical.
items.exampleCN: 同化可以是文化的，也可以是生理的。

items.example: An assimilated group speaks the majority language.
items.exampleCN: 被同化的群体说多数人的语言。

derivatives.meaning: the process of becoming part of a whole
